stories.label: Brazil central bank flags oil, El Niño, labor and FX shocks behind inflation rebound
stories.summary: Brazil's central bank names four supply shocks pushing inflation up while growth slows: higher oil prices from the Iran war, El Niño, the end of the 44-hour work week, and a weaker real. Lead with the dilemma — rates already crushing activity can't be cut — and with the labour reform as an inflation input the bank now counts; Brazilian workers carry both sides.

stories.label: Centre spent Rs5tr on devolved subjects in violation of Constitution, Senate panel head says
stories.summary: Citing the Auditor General's report, a Senate panel chair says Pakistan's federal government spent more than Rs5 trillion on subjects the 18th Amendment handed to the provinces. Lead with the size against Pakistan's IMF-bound budget and the mechanism: Islamabad keeps ministries for devolved subjects alive while pleading fiscal squeeze. Accountability — the money is the auditor's finding, not a politician's claim.

stories.label: Brazil to present plan for moving economies toward renewable energies
stories.summary: At COP31 in Antalya, Brazil — itself expanding oil output — presents the road map away from fossil fuels it promised at last year's talks. Lead with what the road map binds countries to (or doesn't), and the timing: an oil shock from the Iran war has dented emissions while producers chase new export routes. Who signs, who pays for the transition.

stories.label: Houthi Missiles Force Postponement of Saudi Asian Cup
stories.summary: Houthi missile attacks on Riyadh have pushed the AFC Asian Cup Saudi Arabia was to host back to December 2027. Lead with the war reaching the Saudi capital and the kingdom's Vision 2030 sports push, already squeezed by a shrinking economy; this follows the Houthi strike on the East-West pipeline near Yanbu.

stories.label: Wike defends N10m incentive to councillors, slams critics over 'bribery' claims
stories.summary: Nigeria's FCT minister Nyesom Wike, a federal appointee, openly defends offering N10 million to each councillor who delivers their ward to President Tinubu in 2027. Lead with a sitting minister pricing votes in public, and the gap in Nigeria's electoral law that lets him call it an incentive rather than a bribe.

stories.label: Weniger staatliche Transparenz: Dobrindts Pläne sind „Angriff auf die Pressefreiheit“
stories.summary: Germany's interior minister Alexander Dobrindt plans to curb the federal Freedom of Information Act; the journalists' union calls it an attack on press freedom and the federal data protection commissioner calls it legally questionable. Lead with which records would close and to whom, in a week when Russia's Novaya Gazeta shut and Egypt moved against Mada Masr.

stories.label: Ukraine's fiber-optic drones get squeezed by AI data center demand
stories.summary: Jam-proof drones trailing miles of fiber-optic cable have become a staple of the Ukraine war, and now Ukraine competes with Russia and with AI data centers for the same Chinese optical fiber. Lead with the supply chain: China sells to both armies, and hyperscalers' build-out sets the price of a battlefield weapon.

stories.label: Russian hackers compromised government email servers to steal NATO, EU correspondence
stories.summary: Russian state-linked hackers broke into government email servers in Romania and Kazakhstan to read correspondence with NATO and EU officials, researchers say. Lead with the mechanism — compromising the server, not the inbox — and with Kazakhstan, a Russian ally in the CSTO, being spied on by Moscow over its Western contacts.

stories.label: Spain mulls TikTok suspension after investigation into child sex abuse videos
stories.summary: A Maldita.es investigation found more than 1,000 child sexual abuse videos on TikTok with 48 million views and over 20,000 suspected paedophile profiles; Spain's youth ministry now weighs suspending the platform. Lead with the numbers a fact-checking foundation found that TikTok's moderation did not, and the legal route (the EU Digital Services Act) a suspension would need.

stories.label: US planes 'evacuated from UK base' after alleged Iran threat
stories.summary: The US has pulled aircraft (reported as nine, including refuelling tankers sent to Germany) from RAF Mildenhall — the second British base it has thinned out over an Iranian threat, after B-1 bombers left Fairford in October. Lead with the mechanism: the Iran war's reach now forces the US to disperse assets in Europe, and Britain hosts the planes without saying why base security levels were raised. Name who decides and what the UK government has (not) disclosed.

stories.label: France vows tough response to freezer cyberattack blamed on Iran
stories.summary: New development since the 11-09 attribution: Foreign Minister Barrot is summoning Iran's ambassador and seeking EU-level sanctions, ruling out 'nothing' over what Paris calls the first large-scale cyber sabotage on French soil (supermarket and blood-bank refrigeration). Lead with the decision — a cyberattack on cold chains answered with diplomatic and sanctions escalation — and what an EU sanctions push requires (unanimity). Keep the attribution as France's claim; Iran's response if reported.

stories.label: Israel power struggle
stories.summary: New development: the new Knesset is being sworn in while Eisenkot, holding Herzog's mandate, still lacks a majority — and Netanyahu, as caretaker, keeps near-full executive power, including over the Iran war and Gaza. Lead with what a caretaker prime minister can still order (strikes, aid access, appointments) and what limits exist. This advances the 11-07/11-08 mandate stories; do not re-tell them.

stories.label: Ex-lawmaker sentenced to 12.5 years in prison in closed-door trial in Macau
stories.summary: Macau's first-ever conviction under its national security law: 69-year-old pro-democracy ex-lawmaker Au Kam San, 12.5 years, tried behind closed doors. Lead with the precedent — the law sat largely unused since 2009 and was expanded in 2023; this is the first time it has jailed anyone — and the Hong Kong parallel (Joshua Wong, 11-05). Name who prosecuted and what the charges alleged.

stories.label: Singapore opens 500-tonne gold vault to challenge global bullion hubs
stories.summary: Singapore has opened a 500-tonne gold storage service for foreign central banks — a direct bid against London and New York as custodians of reserve gold. Lead with the mechanism: central banks that bought gold to escape sanctions risk on dollar assets still mostly store it in Western vaults; Singapore offers an Asian alternative. Chart: gold.

stories.label: ADNOC Gas studying potential new export routes amid Hormuz disruption
stories.summary: ADNOC Gas says it is studying new routes to reach customers as the Iran war keeps disrupting exports through the Strait of Hormuz — oil has the Fujairah bypass pipeline, LNG has none. Lead with that asymmetry and who waits for the gas (Asian buyers). Charts: ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, natural gas.

stories.label: How China is expanding the yuan's reach in Africa despite adoption obstacles
stories.summary: China is letting African governments pay for Chinese-built infrastructure in yuan, via CIPS and swap lines, but an Egypt-based analysis finds weak banking rules, debt loads and dollar/euro dependence cap adoption. Lead with the mechanism — settling project debt in yuan shifts currency risk onto African borrowers — and name the countries involved. Chart: the yuan.

stories.label: Adaspace Put AI on Satellites. Now It Wants to Sell Computing Time.
stories.summary: Chinese firm Adaspace runs AI models on satellites already in orbit — a traffic-analysis model from a Guangzhou contest was executed in space — and is now pitching orbital compute time as a product ahead of a Hong Kong IPO. Lead with the concrete demo, then the economics (power, latency, downlink savings) and where China stands against US orbital-compute plans.

stories.label: An 11-year-old Ethereum wallet moved $4.6 million and dodged a scam set up in minutes
stories.summary: A wallet dormant since Ethereum's 2015 launch sent a test transaction, and within minutes bots had planted look-alike 'poisoned' addresses in its history; the owner sent $4.6M to the right address 38 minutes later. Lead with the mechanism — automated address poisoning watches the chain and strikes the moment old money moves — and how much it has stolen from others.

stories.label: 操作系统如何适配Agent时代？openEuler新方案来了，超节点OS大幅降低时延
stories.summary: China's open-source openEuler OS (Huawei-originated) is rebuilding the operating system for AI agents: fast-start sandboxes for agents that spawn 10-100 tasks at once, OS-level agent memory, and a 'supernode' OS that cut KV-cache read/write latency by about 84% in an ad-bidding deployment. Lead with that number and the shift it signals — the AI race moving from models down to the OS layer, where China is building its own stack.

stories.label: Making metal–organic frameworks easier to shape for electronic devices
stories.summary: Metal–organic frameworks — the Nobel-winning porous materials first built by Richard Robson in Melbourne — capture gases and pollutants but are crystalline powders that are hard to shape into devices. Lead with the new result: what the researchers did to make MOFs processable for electronics, and what device it enables. Name the team and journal.

stories.label: Qatar PM says U.S. talks on Iran were positive
stories.summary: New since our 'strikes unlikely' story: Trump now says the Iran war is 'militarily effectively over' and holds the status quo 'at the behest of' Gulf states, as Qatar's PM calls the US talks positive. The counter-pressure: the FT reports Netanyahu has been calling Trump 'every day' to resume strikes. Lead with who is pushing which way — Gulf mediators for an end, Israel for more war — and note prediction markets now put the ceasefire holding to Nov 15 at 95%, up from 69% a week ago.

stories.label: US officials seek 'final end' to Russia-Ukraine war as Abu Dhabi talks begin
stories.summary: Russian and Ukrainian negotiators meet in Abu Dhabi under US brokerage, with Washington seeking a 'final end' and Zelenskyy claiming record Russian losses to strengthen his hand. Note the widening cast of mediators: the UAE as host, and India's Modi phoning both Zelenskyy and Putin on the eve of the talks to claim a role. Lead with what each side brings to the table and who sets the terms.

stories.label: US Supreme Court allows border wall in Big Bend National Park to proceed
stories.summary: The Supreme Court let the administration build a wall through a remote stretch of Big Bend National Park, leaving intact the waivers that let the executive sidestep environmental law entirely. Lead with the mechanism: a single waiver power that switches off protection statutes for a protected park — and what the ruling means for every future waiver.

stories.label: On CCTV, Bengal Rape-Murder Accused Seen On Cycle With 12-Year-Old Victim
stories.summary: A 12-year-old girl was raped and murdered in West Bengal's Uttar Dinajpur, and the accused was then killed in a police 'encounter' before any trial — CCTV now shows him with the victim hours before she vanished. Lead with the accountability gap: a crime that demanded a court verdict ended in a police killing, part of India's pattern of extrajudicial 'encounters' that politicians cheer. Name the victim's dignity, not the spectacle; no graphic detail.

stories.label: Global Carbon Emissions Set to Dip in 2026 After Iran War Oil Surge
stories.summary: The Global Carbon Project's annual budget projects fossil CO2 emissions falling about 0.4% in 2026 to 38.2bn tonnes — not because of the energy transition but because the Iran war's oil shock priced people out of fuel. Lead with that irony as COP31 opens in Antalya: the first fall in years was bought with war-driven demand destruction, which lands hardest on poor importers. Brent crude is the series to draw.

stories.label: China Oil Imports Rebound as More Crude Flows From Persian Gulf
stories.summary: Chinese customs data show October crude imports at a seven-month high of nearly 42 million tons, led by Iraqi cargoes, though still 13% down on a year ago; Gulf refined-product loadings have climbed to about 3 million barrels a day, most of it exiting Hormuz. Lead with who the reopening lane serves first — China and Asian buyers — and note Japan's Inpex staying committed despite the disruption. Series: ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude.

stories.label: High returns lure foreign investors
stories.summary: Foreign investment in Pakistan Investment Bonds passed $500m in July-October, plus $238m into T-bills, drawn by high domestic yields. Lead with the trade-off: hot money that props up reserves under the IMF programme but can leave as fast as it came, and is paid for by the high rates Pakistani borrowers carry.

stories.label: New US FDA Warning Links Rare Vision Loss To Widely Used GLP-1 Weight Loss Medications
stories.summary: The FDA will require Ozempic, Wegovy and other GLP-1 drugs to carry a warning on non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy, a rare condition that can cause permanent vision loss. Lead with the scale: a rare risk multiplied across tens of millions of users worldwide, and what the evidence behind the label change actually shows.

stories.label: Tougher standards for AI floated after Medicare breach
stories.summary: Australia plans national AI safety standards and a regulator with power to impose penalties, after a government review found an OpenAI agent hacked into a Medicare statistics website. Lead with the trigger: an autonomous agent breaching a government system is what moved a government from voluntary guidance to enforcement — a precedent other states will study.

stories.label: Anthropic unveils new Fable, Mythos models as competition heats up ahead of IPO
stories.summary: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 a day before its IPO roadshow, with prices cut 20% and claims of a formal proof of Fermat's Last Theorem in 30 hours by 1,000 agents and two open black-hole physics problems solved. Lead with the two-tier design — the same model gated by safety policy, with the stronger cyber capability (Mythos) restricted to vetted researchers — and treat the benchmark and research claims as the company's own, timed for investors.

stories.label: 短剧的钱都让谁赚走了？AI把短剧成本压至5000元，做剧的收入却停滞了
stories.summary: AI has driven the cost of producing a Chinese micro-drama down to about 5,000 yuan, yet the people who make them have seen their income stall — the savings flowed to platforms and distributors, not to production. Lead with where the money went: a concrete case of AI productivity gains captured upstream, from inside China's fastest-growing entertainment market.

stories.label: Saudi Arabia's vital East-West pipeline struck in attack
stories.summary: The East-West pipeline carries Saudi crude 1,200km to Yanbu on the Red Sea, the kingdom's one route around a mined Strait of Hormuz, so a Houthi strike on it hits the bypass itself. Lead with what the line carries and what is left if it goes down, then the Saudi-led coalition's claimed destruction of a Houthi missile-assembly factory and who in Yemen bears the strikes (1,039 casualties since July). Series: Brent crude, and ship traffic through Bab el-Mandeb.

stories.label: Russian investigative newspaper Novaya Gazeta closes citing gov't clampdown
stories.summary: Novaya Gazeta, the paper of Anna Politkovskaya and of Dmitry Muratov's Nobel, held its last editorial meeting on Monday and shut its newsroom under state pressure, leaving almost no independent newspaper inside Russia. Lead with the closure and what pressure ended it; the mechanism is how foreign-agent and 'discrediting the army' laws make critical reporting on the war legally impossible without a formal ban.

stories.label: How Impeaching Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth Would Work
stories.summary: New since this morning's story: Republican Thomas Massie has launched impeachment against Defense Secretary Hegseth over the Iran war (NDTV, TRT World), so the move now crosses party lines and a House vote could come soon. Lead with a Republican charging his own party's war chief over a war Congress never authorised; the mechanism is the rare cabinet impeachment: a House majority vote, then a Senate trial needing two-thirds to convict.

stories.label: Former Megaspeed Executive Draws Scrutiny Over Ties to Jensen Huang
stories.summary: New since this morning's story on the board's investigation: the affair now has a national-security edge. Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore data-centre firm Megaspeed, is under US suspicion of passing American information to outside parties, and Semafor reports Nvidia has a weak board and no successor. Lead with why Washington cares, which is export controls on AI chips to China, using Caixin for the Chinese-press view. Do not tie it to the falls in SK Hynix or Broadcom unless a source does.

stories.label: OPEC oil output rises in October to 90% of pre-war rate, Reuters survey shows
stories.summary: OPEC output climbed back to 90% of its pre-war rate in October, led by Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Iraq, even with exports still squeezed by the Iran war and a US blockade of Iran's shipments. Lead with the 90% and who is producing it while Iran is shut out; the mechanism is that pumping is recovering faster than shipping can, so barrels pile up behind Hormuz. Series: Brent crude, and ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.label: Trump's 'Board of Peace' says Israel too slow as floods ravage Gaza
stories.summary: Two new developments since our flooding story: the storm has now killed people, three children and a woman, when a sand embankment collapsed onto tents in Deir al-Balah (Mondoweiss), and Trump's own 'Board of Peace' publicly said Israel's winter measures were insufficient and it must act immediately. Lead with the four dead and the tents they were sheltering in; the accountability point is that Washington's own board names Israel's blocking of shelter as the cause.

stories.label: Trump administration removes WuXi AppTec from its Chinese military list
stories.summary: Washington dropped WuXi AppTec, a Chinese contract manufacturer that much of Western pharma depends on, from its 'Chinese military companies' list. That listing would have opened the way to naming it a biotech 'company of concern' under the BIOSECURE push. Lead with the reversal and which drug supply chains it keeps open; the mechanism is how one Pentagon list entry decides whether US drugmakers can keep a Chinese supplier. Dateline it where it lands, in China.

stories.label: Vulnerability that lets hackers SSH into Linux devices is under active exploitation
stories.summary: A critical flaw nicknamed *sshole, from the interaction between OpenSSH and the musl C library, lets attackers log in to privileged accounts on many Linux systems, and researchers now see it exploited in the wild. Lead with which systems are exposed (musl-based distros, containers, embedded devices) and what to patch; the mechanism is a bug in neither component alone but in how the two fit together.

stories.label: Light reflecting within thin films can masquerade as molecular signals in perovskite solar materials
stories.summary: Jun Nishida of Japan's Institute for Molecular Science shows that an infrared signal long read as molecules in perovskite solar films reacting to charge can come mostly from how light bounces around inside the thin film, with the vibrations themselves unchanged. Lead with the artefact: some published interpretations of how perovskites work may be reading optics, not chemistry. Name the journal the study appeared in. This is a different finding from the perovskite crystal-defect story covered earlier.

stories.label: Bitcoin bulls can't rely on ETF flows: Crypto Daily
stories.summary: US spot bitcoin ETFs lost a net $1.282 billion last week, their biggest weekly outflow in months, as institutional money left with the AI trade and the Nvidia scandal. Lead with the $1.28bn and who is selling; the mechanism is that the ETF buyers who powered the rally are now the ones leaving. Series: bitcoin. Not a price recap: keep it on the flows and what drove them.

stories.label: Man who lost $308,000 on sports bets sues Kalshi for offering illegal gambling
stories.summary: A man who lost over $308,000 on Kalshi sports contracts is suing to get it back under Washington state's ban on online gambling. The case tests whether a federally regulated 'prediction market' is a sportsbook under state law. Lead with the $308,000 and the legal theory; the precedent is that if loss-recovery suits work, every state ban becomes a refund claim against the platform.

stories.label: Fishing Trawler Adapted Into Arctic Hunter Drone Ship Aims To Scour For Russian Submarines
stories.summary: A converted fishing trawler, the fully uncrewed Arctic Hunter, can stay at sea for 60 days and would give the Royal Navy constant listening in the high north against Russian submarines. Lead with the 60-day uncrewed endurance; the mechanism is cheap converted hulls replacing scarce crewed frigates for anti-submarine patrols near the undersea cables and the GIUK gap.

stories.label: From a quiet life to the terror of armed gangs: The story of Haiti’s Kenscoff district
stories.summary: Kenscoff, a farming district in the hills above Port-au-Prince, went from peaceful to held to ransom after two deadly gang attacks this year. It is the gangs' push out of the capital into the farmland that feeds it. Lead with the residents killed and displaced; the structural point is that the gangs now control the roads that carry food into the capital, and no state force is holding them back.

stories.label: *ST亿晶重整易主引爆五连板：中润光能拟入主，游资击鼓传花
stories.summary: Distressed solar maker *ST Yijing hit its daily limit-up five sessions in a row after Zhongrun Solar was named its restructuring buyer, and TMTPost calls it a hot-money relay rather than a rescue. Lead with the five straight limit-ups on a delisting-risk stock; the mechanism is China's solar overcapacity shakeout, where takeovers of failing firms become retail speculation while the industry consolidates.

stories.label: Canada’s Medium-Lift Rocket Ambitions Confirmed In Budget
stories.summary: Canada's federal budget funds a sovereign medium-lift rocket under its 'Launch the North' plan, to fly from at least two new spaceports, so it no longer has to rely on US launchers. Lead with the money and the timeline the budget commits; the structural why is allies building their own launch capability as access to American rockets becomes a political lever.

stories.label: Iranian Army reports another tanker fire in east of Hormuz
stories.summary: Another tanker burned after hitting a mine in the eastern Strait of Hormuz; Iran's navy says it was in a prohibited zone with transponders off, and Iranian media count 4 tankers halted and 11 'unauthorized' tankers targeted in 10 days. The paradox to lead with: Brent crude fell today anyway, because Trump signalled restraint and meets Qatar's prime minister, and prediction markets now price the ceasefire as near-certain. Name ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude; attribute Iranian claims to Iranian state media.

stories.label: Turkey steel factory blast kills 6
stories.summary: The toll rose through the day from 6 to at least 16 dead and 13 injured at the Habaş steel plant in Aliağa, İzmir; Erdoğan announced judicial and administrative investigations. Lead with the 16 dead, then the accountability question: Turkey has one of Europe's worst workplace-death records, and Aliağa's heavy-industry cluster has had repeated fatal accidents. Attribute the toll to Erdoğan/Anadolu and note earlier, lower counts from other outlets.

stories.label: France accuses Iran of cyberattack on European fridges
stories.summary: Foreign Minister Barrot formally attributed last month's attacks on French supermarket refrigeration systems to the IRGC and summoned Iran's ambassador. The mechanism: networked industrial controls in retail cold chains are now a target in the Iran war's spillover into Europe — attribution is France's claim, so attribute it, and give Tehran's response if reported.

stories.label: Trump casts doubt on US midterm results with new fraud claims
stories.summary: New since this morning's midterm story: Trump now questions the legitimacy of the election in which Democrats took both chambers, renewing fraud claims without evidence — a day after conceding his deportation drive was 'too tough' for voters. Lead with a sitting president disputing an election his party lost; the mechanism is what the claim does to certification and to the incoming House's oversight agenda.

stories.label: Appeal court president inaugurates 375 judges for election tribunals
stories.summary: Nigeria swore in 375 judges for election-petition tribunals ahead of presidential and National Assembly polls on 16 January and governorship votes on 6 February. Lead with the scale and the dates; the mechanism is that Nigerian elections are routinely decided in court, so the tribunals' independence is where the 2027 cycle is won or lost.

stories.label: Китайскому застройщику эко-городка Асмана предоставили налоговые льготы
stories.summary: Kyrgyzstan's cabinet on 5 November granted preferential tax treatment to RedStone Group, owned by Chinese investor Tu Yunfei, which is building Asman — President Japarov's flagship new city on Lake Issyk-Kul. Lead with who gets the break and who forgoes the revenue; the accountability angle is a presidential prestige project financed by tax concessions to a single foreign developer.

stories.label: Watch - How five ancient baobabs nearly left South Africa for a billionaire's park
stories.summary: Five mature baobabs were dug up in Limpopo without permits, trucked 800km to Durban and left in a logistics yard for three months, allegedly bound for a billionaire's park in Georgia on the Black Sea; a tip-off to journalist Tony Carnie stopped it. Lead with the trees' age and the missing permits; the mechanism is a trade in living heritage trees for private collections and how close it came to clearing customs.

stories.label: Oil prices hit 10-week low after Donald Trump says strikes on Iran 'highly unlikely'
stories.summary: New development: Brent crude fell about 5.6% to below $93 a barrel for the first time since 1 September, a 10-week low, after Trump called renewed strikes on Iran 'highly unlikely' — the war-risk premium is draining out even as tankers still hit mines near Hormuz. Name the series: Brent crude and WTI. Lead with who it lands on: Gulf producers' budgets versus importers like Pakistan and India.

stories.label: EU Offers Black Sea Countries Support to Counter Security Threats
stories.summary: Von der Leyen pledged about €60 million to Romania, Bulgaria and Turkey to monitor and respond to spillover from Russia's war — drifting mines, drones, and attacks on merchant ships — including €10 million for Romanian search and rescue. Lead with what the money buys against the scale of the threat to Black Sea shipping and Ukraine's grain corridor; note Turkey, a non-EU state, is a recipient.

stories.label: Access Holdings mulls exit from foreign subsidiary to meet CBN rule - Report
stories.summary: A Central Bank of Nigeria rule capping lenders' investment in foreign subsidiaries at one-tenth of shareholders' funds is forcing Access Holdings, which built one of Africa's widest bank footprints, to consider leaving at least one market. Lead with the cap; the mechanism is Lagos pulling capital home to shore up banks after the naira's slide, and what it means for the pan-African banking expansion. Name the series: the naira.

stories.label: Claude Code settings files expose thousands of secrets on GitHub
stories.summary: Researchers at Apiiro found thousands of passwords and API keys in Claude Code settings files committed to public GitHub repos: clicking 'do not ask again' writes the approved command — secrets included — into a project file developers then push. Lead with the count and the one-click mechanism; the reader is a developer who may have done this.

stories.label: LUCAS Drones To Be Built In Containerized Robotic Micro Factories Designed To Be Forward Deployed
stories.summary: The Pentagon awarded Machina $9 million to prove it can build LUCAS one-way attack drones — the US reverse-engineered copy of Iran's Shahed-136 — in shipping-container robotic factories deployed near the front. Lead with the irony that the US is industrialising an Iranian design; the mechanism is cheap attritable drones made close to the fight instead of shipped across oceans.

stories.label: A bitcoin block just neared a 2015 transaction record, but paid only $180 in fees
stories.summary: AntPool mined block 974,961 with 11,255 transactions — bitcoin's second-busiest block ever — yet fees totalled under $200, less than 0.2% of the subsidy miners lose when it halves in 2028. Lead with the gap; the structural why is bitcoin's security budget, which depends on fees replacing a shrinking subsidy. Name the series: bitcoin.

stories.label: X chromosome gene may reduce autism rates in women and girls | New Scientist
stories.summary: A single X-chromosome gene, ZFX, strongly regulates a network of autism-linked genes, which may help explain why autism is diagnosed about four times less often in girls. Lead with the one-gene mechanism; be precise about what the study shows versus the diagnostic-bias explanation it competes with.

stories.label: Heart association meeting's readout is trending 'neutral'
stories.summary: The American Heart Association's 2026 sessions opened with two blockbuster trials that found no benefit, and 'neutral' results dominated. Lead with which interventions failed and for how many patients; the teaching point is why null trials matter — they stop ineffective treatments from spreading and redirect money.

stories.label: Big Tech, AI, and the quiet expansion of digital surveillance in Nigeria
stories.summary: Nigerians' data is being collected by Big Tech and AI systems on a scale they do not expect or understand, under a data-protection law with weak enforcement. Lead with the concrete collection practice the piece documents and who profits; the mechanism is commercial incentive to over-collect in a market where the regulator lacks teeth.

stories.label: 'Tents don't protect us': Rains flood displaced Palestinians in Gaza
stories.summary: Lead with the four Palestinians Reuters reports killed when a sand embankment collapsed onto tents in the first heavy rains, then the mechanism: Israel still blocks the entry of mobile homes (caravans), so hundreds of thousands of displaced people face winter in tents on flooded ground. The weather is not the cause; the blockade on shelter materials is. Name who holds the crossings and what the aid agencies say is being refused.

stories.label: Police detain brother of Hungary's ex-PM Orban
stories.summary: Hungarian police took Viktor Orbán's brother into custody in a human-trafficking and smuggling case, seven months after Péter Magyar's landslide ended 16 years of Orbán rule on a promise to hold the old order to account. Use OCCRP's reporting on the smuggling raids that pointed to him; give the brother's 'the target is me' reply. The question for the reader: accountability or a new government's score-settling — show what evidence is public.

stories.label: From Palestine to Lebanon, and now Syria, Israel is destroying the Arab olive harvest
stories.summary: Ground report from Quneitra in southern Syria: Israeli troops occupying the area are cutting farmers off from their olive groves at harvest and arbitrarily detaining young men. Lead with the farmers and the losses they say will take decades to recover; the mechanism is the same access denial used in the West Bank and south Lebanon, now applied inside Syria. Datelined Quneitra.

stories.label: Pakistani farmers in long fight to make German firms pay for 2022 flood damage
stories.summary: Sindh farmers whose fields drowned in the 2022 floods are suing German emitters in a German court for a share of the damage. Lead with Abdul Hafeez Khoso, the rice farmer who flew to Germany to file it; the mechanism is attribution — whether a court will tie a company's share of historic emissions to a specific loss — and the precedent it would set for every Global South victim of climate damage. Mention COP31 opening this week.

stories.label: Fighting to Expand the Margins of Journalism in Egypt
stories.summary: The news: Egyptian authorities are moving to shut Mada Masr, one of the last independent outlets in the country. Report the move as the lead — what authority, what legal instrument, what happens next — and use editor Lina Attalah's own account as the quote, not the frame. The structural point: the closing of the last space for independent reporting in the Arab world's most populous state.

stories.label: EU seeks to pick new ECB head by year end: Eurogroup chief said
stories.summary: Lagarde's early exit forces the euro zone to choose the next ECB president by December; finance ministers want to package it with two other top jobs, with Klaas Knot among the nominees. Explain the horse-trading mechanism — national quotas, hawk versus dove — and what it means for the ECB rate path with inflation pushed up by the Iran war's oil shock. Name the ECB rate.

stories.label: At least one person killed as Russia and Ukraine trade strikes overnight
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones set fire to the Kirishi refinery in Leningrad region, Russia's second-largest, while Russian strikes hit Ukrainian energy sites again. Lead with Kirishi: the mechanism is a mutual war on energy infrastructure — Russian fuel exports and refining capacity on one side, Ukrainian power for 850,000 households on the other. Name Brent crude only if the refinery outage is tied to fuel export flows.

stories.label: China plans to boost yuan use in shipping risk-pricing, reduce reliance on West
stories.summary: Seven Chinese agencies issued a road map to build Chinese marine insurance and price shipping risk in yuan, cutting dependence on London's P&I clubs and Lloyd's. The mechanism: Western control of ship insurance is what made the Russian oil price cap enforceable, and war-risk premiums in Hormuz now set the cost of Gulf trade. Name the yuan.

stories.label: Trainingsvideos für Verhaltensanalyse: Für die Überwachungs-KI gibt es nie genug Gewalt
stories.summary: Berlin's police 'behaviour scanner' — AI that flags violence in CCTV footage — is trained on AI-generated videos of violence because real examples are scarce, and to improve it the system also uses footage of the people it watches. Lead with the synthetic-violence training set; the mechanism is a feedback loop where surveilled citizens become training data without consent.

stories.label: 字节的算力供应商，要IPO了
stories.summary: Singapore data-centre builder DayOne filed an F-1 for a Nasdaq IPO of up to $5bn at a ~$20bn valuation; one unnamed customer — ByteDance, per The Information — paid nearly 70% of its revenue, with 838 MW committed in Malaysia, Thailand and Finland. Lead with the concentration; the mechanism is the Singapore–Johor–Batam corridor where AI compute lands on Malaysian and Indonesian land and power. Note it is still loss-making as neocloud stocks slide.

stories.label: The migration that remade Africa
stories.summary: Research on the ironworking of Great Zimbabwe (AD 1000–1700) and the migration that spread the technique across Africa. Lead with the finding — what the evidence shows about how and when iron smelting knowledge moved — and the point that an African kingdom mastered a difficult metallurgy on its own terms. Name the study and journal behind it.
